title: Coal Miners Fight for Health Benefits as Lung Disease Cases Rise
subtitle: Many retired workers face long legal battles to receive support for a condition caused by years of breathing coal dust.

summary.en: Cases of black lung disease among coal miners have reached a nearly 50-year high. Many retired workers are struggling to get federal benefits due to long and difficult legal appeals. Coal companies often challenge these claims, forcing miners to wait years for financial and medical support. A recent government report highlights that thousands of miners face delays and financial stress during this process. Lawmakers are now looking at new ways to improve the system for these workers.
summary.zh: 煤礦工人的黑肺病病例已達到近五十年來的新高。許多退休工人因漫長且艱難的法律申訴，難以取得聯邦補助。煤礦公司經常對這些申請提出異議，迫使礦工等待數年才能獲得經濟與醫療支援。一份政府最新報告指出，數千名礦工在此過程中面臨延宕與經濟壓力。立法者目前正研擬新方案，以改善該制度來協助這些勞工。

paragraphs.en: For 38 years, Josh Armes worked as a coal miner in West Virginia and Virginia. Today, at 74 years old, he lives with a serious health condition known as black lung disease. Medically called coal workers’ pneumoconiosis, this illness is caused by breathing in coal dust over long periods, which causes permanent damage to the lungs. For the past four years, Mr. Armes has needed an oxygen tank to breathe and must use an inhaler to help when he struggles to get enough air. Even with this help, his daily life is very limited.
paragraphs.zh: 喬許．阿姆斯（Josh Armes）在西維吉尼亞州與維吉尼亞州擔任煤礦工人長達三十八年。如今七十四歲的他，正飽受一種稱為黑肺病的嚴重健康問題所苦。醫學上稱此病為煤礦工人塵肺症，這是因為長期吸入煤塵，導致肺部受到永久性損害。過去四年來，阿姆斯先生必須依賴氧氣瓶呼吸，並在氣喘不過來時使用吸入器輔助。即便有這些協助，他的日常生活仍受到極大限制。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Armes is not alone in his struggle. According to data published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, cases of black lung disease are rising, reaching a nearly 50-year high. The federal black lung program was created in 1969 to provide miners who are disabled by the disease with money and medical benefits. However, many families are finding that getting this support is becoming increasingly difficult.
paragraphs.zh: 阿姆斯先生並非唯一面臨此困境的人。根據發表在《美國呼吸與重症照護醫學期刊》上的數據顯示，黑肺病病例正持續攀升，達到近五十年來的新高。聯邦黑肺病計畫於一九六九年設立，旨在為因該疾病而喪失勞動能力的礦工提供經濟與醫療補助。然而，許多家庭發現要取得這項支援變得越來越困難。

paragraphs.en: In 2014, Mr. Armes received notice that the federal benefits he had been receiving for more than three years were being challenged by a coal company. For the last 12 years, he and his family have been caught in a long legal process, trying to get their benefits back while his health continues to get worse. His daughter, Crystal Armes, says the process is very hard. She explains that families often have to pay for expensive medical tests themselves and must find a lawyer to help them fight the coal companies in court.
paragraphs.zh: 二〇一四年，阿姆斯先生收到通知，指他已領取超過三年的聯邦補助正遭到一家煤礦公司提出異議。過去十二年來，他和家人陷入漫長的法律程序中，試圖在健康狀況持續惡化的同時爭取回補助金。他的女兒克莉絲朵．阿姆斯（Crystal Armes）表示，這個過程非常艱辛。她解釋說，家庭往往必須自行負擔昂貴的醫療檢測費用，還得聘請律師協助在法庭上與煤礦公司抗爭。

paragraphs.en: According to a report from the Government Accountability Office (GAO) released in May, the system is failing many miners. The report was requested by Democratic senators who want to see changes to the law. The data shows that between 2013 and 2024, 40% of approved claims were disputed, usually by the coal companies themselves. The report noted that the average length of an appealed claim is three years or more. During this time, many miners feel that the companies are simply waiting for them to give up or die so they do not have to pay.
paragraphs.zh: 根據美國政府稽核處（GAO）於五月發布的一份報告，該制度讓許多礦工感到失望。這份報告是由希望推動修法的民主黨參議員所要求。數據顯示，在二〇一三年至二〇二四年期間，有百分之四十的核准申請遭到異議，且通常是由煤礦公司本身提出。報告指出，申訴案件的平均處理時間長達三年以上。在這段期間，許多礦工認為公司只是在等待他們放棄或離世，這樣就不必支付賠償。

paragraphs.en: Some miners have even been forced to pay back money they already received. The GAO report found that between January 2013 and mid-August 2024, 390 people who were initially approved for benefits had their claims denied after an appeal. This left them responsible for paying back the money they had already spent on medical care. Crystal Armes believes the law should be changed so that companies cannot appeal after benefits have been awarded. She argues that the current system puts too much pressure on the sick miner to prove they are ill, even after doctors have confirmed the diagnosis.
paragraphs.zh: 有些礦工甚至被迫償還已經領取的補助金。政府稽核處的報告發現，在二〇一三年一月至二〇二四年八月中旬期間，有三百九十名最初獲准領取補助的人，在申訴後被撤銷資格。這導致他們必須償還已經花在醫療照護上的費用。克莉絲朵．阿姆斯認為法律應該修改，禁止公司在補助核發後提出申訴。她主張，現行制度將過大的壓力加諸在病患礦工身上，要求他們證明自己生病，即便醫師早已確認診斷結果。

paragraphs.en: “I can’t figure out one thing. They sent me a paper that said I got first- and second-stage black lung. That ought to be enough, or do you have to be dead?” Josh Armes said. His frustration is shared by many others in the industry. The GAO report highlights that miners believe the companies are using these long delays as a way to avoid their responsibilities. While the Trump administration has moved to support the coal industry, the human cost of the work remains a major issue for those who spent their lives in the mines.
paragraphs.zh: 「我有一件事想不通。他們寄給我的文件說我得了第一期和第二期黑肺病。這樣難道還不夠嗎？還是說非得要死了才算數？」喬許．阿姆斯說道。他的挫折感也是業界許多人的共同心聲。政府稽核處的報告強調，礦工們認為公司正利用這些漫長的延宕作為規避責任的手段。儘管川普（Donald Trump）政府採取了支持煤炭產業的立場，但對於那些奉獻一生在礦坑工作的人來說，這份工作所付出的生命代價仍是一個重大議題。

paragraphs.en: As of the 2025 fiscal year, about 22,500 people—including miners, their survivors, and their dependents—were receiving benefits. Despite this, the process remains a source of great stress for families like the Armes family. They continue to wait for a final decision, hoping that their long fight will eventually lead to the support they were promised. For now, the future of the federal black lung program remains a topic of debate, with lawmakers looking for ways to make the system fairer and faster for the people who need it most.
paragraphs.zh: 截至二〇二五會計年度，約有兩萬兩千五百人，包括礦工、遺屬及其受扶養人，正在領取補助。儘管如此，這個過程對阿姆斯一家這樣的家庭來說，仍是巨大的壓力來源。他們持續等待最終裁決，希望漫長的抗爭最終能換來當初承諾的支援。目前，聯邦黑肺病計畫的未來仍是辯論焦點，立法者正尋求各種方式，讓制度對最需要的人來說能更公平、更快速。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To formally question the legality or validity of something, such as a claim or decision.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 質疑（合法性或有效性），在此指法律上的抗告或異議。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「挑戰」，這裡指法律程序上的異議。文中：For the 2014, Mr. Armes received notice that the federal benefits he had been receiving for more than three years were being challenged by a coal company.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To argue against or contest the truth or validity of a claim.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 爭議、對抗；在此指公司拒絕承認礦工的賠償申請。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（爭議），這裡作動詞的被動態。文中：The data shows that between 2013 and 2024, 40% of approved claims were disputed, usually by the coal companies themselves.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Referring to a legal claim that is being reviewed or contested after an initial decision.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（上訴），這裡修飾名詞 claim。文中：The report noted that the average length of an appealed claim is three years or more.

sources.title: ‘Do you have to be dead?’: US coalminers plead for benefits as black-lung disease cases surge

quiz.question: According to the GAO report, what is a specific consequence for miners whose benefit claims are denied after an appeal?

options.A: They must immediately stop receiving all medical treatments.
options.B: They are required to return funds that were previously spent on medical care.
options.C: They are permanently banned from applying for federal aid again.
options.D: They must pay a fine to the coal company for filing an unsuccessful claim.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第五段，GAO 報告指出，有 390 人在初步核准後，因上訴被駁回而被迫償還已花費在醫療照護上的補助金。選項 A 錯誤，文中未提及停止治療；選項 C 錯誤，文中未提到永久禁止申請；選項 D 錯誤，文中提到的是償還補助金，而非支付罰款給煤礦公司。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the coal companies' strategy regarding the legal appeals process?

options.A: They are primarily concerned with ensuring that only truly sick miners receive funds.
options.B: They believe that the current federal program is too generous to the miners' families.
options.C: They may be intentionally prolonging legal battles to discourage miners from pursuing their claims.
options.D: They are working closely with the government to reform the application process for faster results.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段與第六段，報告指出許多礦工認為公司利用漫長的延遲（平均三年以上）作為手段，等待礦工放棄或過世，以規避支付責任。選項 A 不正確，因為公司行為被視為規避責任；選項 B 文中未提及公司對補助金額的看法；選項 D 與文意相反，公司是在挑戰補助而非合作改革。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'disputed' mean in the context of the miners' claims?

options.B: Discussed in an open public forum.
options.D: Ignored or forgotten by the authorities.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在第四段中，提到 40% 的核准申請被 'disputed'，結合後文提到煤礦公司在法庭上與礦工對抗，可知此處意指「提出異議」或「質疑」。選項 B 不符語境；選項 C 與文意完全相反；選項 D 不正確，因為這些申請是被煤礦公司積極介入挑戰的，而非被忽略。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding the federal black lung program?

options.A: The program has successfully eliminated black lung disease among coal miners.
options.B: The program provides enough financial support that miners no longer need to work.
options.C: The program is currently failing to provide timely and reliable support to sick miners due to legal obstacles.
options.D: The program is being expanded to cover all types of respiratory illnesses caused by industrial work.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文核心在於探討黑肺病補助計畫雖存在，但因煤礦公司頻繁的法律挑戰與程序延宕，導致礦工在爭取應得補助時面臨巨大壓力與困難。選項 A 錯誤，病例反而上升；選項 B 與文中提到的困境矛盾；選項 D 超出了文章討論的範圍，文章僅聚焦於黑肺病。
